# Configure the AI Inference Gateway

This page describes how to configure the AI Inference Gateway on Kubernetes. You register model services, define an inference pool, and deploy a gateway that routes agent requests to those models. To learn how the gateway works, refer to [Govern model access with the AI Inference Gateway](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/model-access).

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Background

An AI Inference Gateway on Kubernetes uses three kinds of objects:

| Object | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Model services | Pods annotated with `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-role: inference-model`. Consul registers them as model upstreams that gateways discover in the catalog. |
| [`InferencePoolConfig`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/ai/inferencepoolconfig) | Defines the gateway's processor, failover, PII, and telemetry settings. |
| [`InferenceGateway`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/ai/inferencegateway) | Deploys the gateway. It references one `InferencePoolConfig`. |

For each `InferenceGateway`, the controller creates a Deployment, a Service, and an [`inference-gateway` configuration entry](/consul/docs/reference/config-entry/inference-gateway) from the referenced pool. Consul registers the gateway under the `InferenceGateway` name.

## Workflow

Complete the following steps:

1. Register model services.
1. Define an inference pool.
1. Deploy the gateway.
1. Authorize traffic.
1. Connect agents to the gateway.
1. Verify routing.

You can add failover, PII protection, and tracing to the pool at any time. Refer to [Add optional pool settings](#add-optional-pool-settings).

## Requirements

- Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric installed with `ai.enabled` and `ai.inferenceGateway.enabled` set to `true`. Refer to [Install Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/install).
- Envoy 1.38.2 or later. Consul refuses to start an AI Inference Gateway with an older Envoy binary.
- One or more model services that serve an API in a supported protocol.

## Register model services

Annotate the pod template of each model service. The gateway discovers models from these registrations.

<CodeBlockConfig highlight="4-9">

```yaml
template:
  metadata:
    annotations:
      consul.hashicorp.com/connect-inject: "true"
      consul.hashicorp.com/ai-role: inference-model
      consul.hashicorp.com/ai-inference-model-protocol: openai
      consul.hashicorp.com/ai-inference-model-path: /v1
      consul.hashicorp.com/service-meta-capabilities: "chat,summarize"
      consul.hashicorp.com/service-meta-priority_chat: "0"
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

The annotations set the following values:

- `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-inference-model-protocol`: The API dialect the model serves. Set `openai`, `anthropic`, or `passthrough`. Defaults to `openai`.
- `consul.hashicorp.com/ai-inference-model-path`: The base path of the model API. Defaults to `/v1`.
- `consul.hashicorp.com/service-meta-capabilities`: A comma-separated list of the capabilities the model serves.
- `consul.hashicorp.com/service-meta-priority_<capability>`: The model's rank for one capability. Lower values have higher priority, and `0` is the primary tier. Models with the same rank share a tier and are load balanced. A model without a rank sorts last. Because the rank is per capability, one model can be primary for one capability and a backup for another.

You can also set `consul.hashicorp.com/service-meta-model_family` to name the concrete upstream model. The gateway applies it to a request whose model is `auto`.

## Define the inference pool

Create an `InferencePoolConfig` that attaches to the gateway with `parentRefs`. The following minimal pool sets the processor to fail closed, which is also the default.

<CodeBlockConfig filename="inference-pool.yaml">

```yaml
apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1
kind: InferencePoolConfig
metadata:
  name: travel-pool
  namespace: default
spec:
  enabled: true
  parentRefs:
    - kind: InferenceGateway
      name: travel-inference
  processor:
    failureMode: closed
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

The controller applies only the `processor`, `routing.fallback`, `policy.pii`, and `observability` fields. Other fields, including `routing.timeout` and `rateLimit`, have no effect. Refer to the [`InferencePoolConfig` reference](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/ai/inferencepoolconfig).

## Deploy the gateway

1. Create an `InferenceGateway` that references the pool.

   <CodeBlockConfig filename="inference-gateway.yaml">

   ```yaml
   apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1
   kind: InferenceGateway
   metadata:
     name: travel-inference
     namespace: default
   spec:
     poolRef:
       name: travel-pool
   ```

   </CodeBlockConfig>

   The gateway listens on port `8443` by default. To use a different port, set `spec.service.ports`. The first port carries inference traffic.

1. Apply both resources.

   ```shell-session
   $ kubectl apply --filename inference-pool.yaml --filename inference-gateway.yaml
   ```

You can also create gateways from Helm with the [`ai.inferenceGateway.gateways`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-ai-inferencegateway-gateways) value. The chart renders one `InferenceGateway` for each entry.

## Authorize traffic

Service intentions decide which agents can call the gateway and which models the gateway can reach. Create one intention that allows each agent to call the gateway, and one that allows the gateway to call each model service.

<CodeBlockConfig filename="inference-intentions.yaml">

```yaml
apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1
kind: ServiceIntentions
metadata:
  name: travel-inference
spec:
  destination:
    name: travel-inference
  sources:
    - name: <agent-service>
      action: allow
---
apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1
kind: ServiceIntentions
metadata:
  name: <model-service>
spec:
  destination:
    name: <model-service>
  sources:
    - name: travel-inference
      action: allow
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

```shell-session
$ kubectl apply --filename inference-intentions.yaml
```

For more information, refer to [Service intentions](/consul/docs/reference/config-entry/service-intentions).

## Connect agents to the gateway

Agents send OpenAI-compatible requests to the gateway over a mesh upstream. Declare the gateway as an upstream on each agent's pod template, using the `InferenceGateway` name and a local port.

```yaml
template:
  metadata:
    annotations:
      consul.hashicorp.com/connect-service-upstreams: "travel-inference:8080"
```

<!-- TODO: Verify that the connect-service-upstreams annotation is the supported way for a workload to reach an AI Inference Gateway, and confirm the request path an agent sends, such as /v1/chat/completions. The processor lives in the consul-ai-apps codebase. -->

The gateway routes each request in one of two modes:

- **Capability routing.** The default. The agent sets the `x-inference-specialization` request header to a capability. The gateway sends the request to the highest-priority tier of models that serve that capability.
- **Body model routing.** Set `processor.bodyModelRouting` to `true` in the pool. The gateway routes on the model named in the request body.

## Verify routing

1. From an agent pod, send a request with a capability header.

   ```shell-session
   $ curl --silent http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions \
       --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
       --header "x-inference-specialization: chat" \
       --data '{"model": "auto", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello."}]}'
   ```

   The gateway returns the model's response.

1. Send the same request without the header. The gateway has no route for it and fails closed with HTTP `503`. A request for a capability that no model serves also returns `503`.

## Add optional pool settings

Add any of the following blocks to the `InferencePoolConfig` `spec`, then apply the pool again.

### Fail over across model tiers

Retry a failed request on the next priority tier. This example retries on server errors and connection failures, tries at most two tiers, and limits each attempt to 30 seconds.

```yaml
routing:
  fallback:
    retryOn: ["5xx", "connect-failure"]
    maxTiers: 2
    perTryTimeout: 30s
```

### Protect PII

Detect and handle personally identifiable information. This example masks email addresses in requests and responses.

```yaml
policy:
  pii:
    scope: both
    defaultAction: mask
    detectors:
      - name: email
```

For detectors, actions, and streaming settings, refer to [Data protection and streaming](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/model-access#data-protection-and-streaming).

### Export traces

Send gateway traces to an OpenTelemetry Collector.

```yaml
observability:
  tracing:
    enabled: true
    sampleRatio: 1
    otlp:
      endpoint: otel-collector:4318
```

For the full setup, refer to [Configure auto-instrumentation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/configure-auto-instrumentation).
